items.title: A humorous social-affective instructional style in generative AI pedagogical agents: effects on cognitive load, immediate learning performance, and learner perceptions
items.summary_en: Generative AI pedagogical agents can provide adaptive instructional dialogue, but their responses may also appear impersonal, overly formal, or insufficiently engaging. One possible design response is to embed instructionally relevant humor into agent–learner interaction. This study examined whether a humorous social-affective instructional style that combined content-related, non-disparaging humor with mild colloquial expression and encouraging language influenced learners’ self-reported cognitive load, immediate post-test performance, and perceived agent value in an online learning activity.
